- Model consistently underestimates prices, especially in early days of the forecast horizon (e.g., first 5–10 days).
- Overestimates after sharp price spikes (e.g., 70+ → 72+), then overshoots and fails to correct downward.
- Underestimates in late forecast period (last 5–10 days), suggesting lag in capturing upward momentum or policy-driven spikes.
- Mean reversion bias: model assumes prices return to historical mean too quickly, missing sustained upward trends.
- Forecast horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts show persistent underestimation, especially when true prices rise above 70.00.
- Model reacts too slowly to recent price increases; fails to “catch up” with recent highs in the 10–15 day window.
- Avoids sharp upward revisions in the final 5–7 days; underestimates final spike (e.g., 72.65, 71.87) when true price rises sharply.
